facts.text: Walden grew from a mill town along the Wallkill River, founded by Jacob Walden in 1813 who built a dam and power station still in use.
The village became a knife‑making hub in the 19th and early 20th centuries, hosting the New York Knife Company (1856), Walden Knife Company (1870s), and Schrade Cutlery (1904).
Schrade Cutlery was the last knife factory in Walden; its 1904 plant burned and closed, leaving ruins behind the Thruway Markets hypermarket.
Walden’s historic industrial corridor runs along the railroad line, with the old Wallkill Valley Railroad spur still operated by Norfolk Southern to serve local businesses.
The Fox Hill Bruderhof Community on Walden’s southern edge houses about 250 members who live and work in local factories and a publishing house.
Millspaugh Furniture, founded in Walden, remains a regional draw for shoppers seeking quality craftsmanship, despite having another outlet in Poughkeepsie.
